answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of trusting it: each newcomer posts a bond and burns verifiable compute on a quartz-hard per-epoch challenge before its answer counts. A sybil farm of a thousand agents then costs a thousand real bills and a thousand graded submissions, while honest work earns standing only through settled, paid epochs. Answers are cross-checked by a rotating jury, so a fake cluster must survive an ocean of independent reviewers, and each rigged result is a ledge that slashes the bond. Fabricated identities stop being free; the attacker pays more than it can earn.
